items.prompt:
A mark that joins a compound modifier before a noun is a:
A) hyphen
B) semicolon
C) period

Which is spelled correctly?
A) separate
B) seperate
C) seperit

Which is spelled correctly?
A) unnecessary
B) unneccessary
C) unecessary

Which phrase is correctly hyphenated?
A) 'a well-known author'
B) 'a well known-author'
C) 'a-well known author'

steps: Compound modifier before noun. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which sentence needs NO hyphen?
A) 'The author is well known.'
B) 'a well known author'
C) 'a five year old child'

steps: Modifier comes after the noun. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which uses a semicolon correctly?
A) 'The vote passed; the crowd cheered.'
B) 'The vote passed; and cheered.'
C) 'The vote passed; loudly.'
items.answer: A) 'The vote passed; the crowd cheered.'

steps: Two independent clauses. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'The vote passed; the crowd cheered.'

items.prompt:
Which sentence is correctly hyphenated and spelled?
A) 'The well-prepared, twenty-one-year-old candidate gave a separate statement.'
B) 'The well prepared, twentyone year old candidate gave a seperate statement.'
C) 'The well-prepared, twenty one year old candidate gave a separate statement.'
items.answer: A) 'The well-prepared, twenty-one-year-old candidate gave a separate statement.'

steps: Compound modifiers + number hyphens + spelling. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'The well-prepared, twenty-one-year-old candidate gave a separate statement.'

items.prompt:
Which sentence is fully correct?
A) 'During the Civil War, that was definitely an unnecessary occurrence.'
B) 'during the civil war, that was definately an unneccessary occurence.'
C) 'In the autumn, those were clearly avoidable mistakes made twice.'
items.answer: A) 'During the Civil War, that was definitely an unnecessary occurrence.'

solution.answer: A) 'During the Civil War, that was definitely an unnecessary occurrence.'
